comm.t: The sage Medhas resumes his story for King Suratha (and the merchant Samādhi). Chapter 3 ended with Mahiṣāsura beheaded (3.42), his army destroyed (3.43) and the gods beginning to praise the Devī (3.44); this chapter gives that praise in full. In recitation the mantra carries the bīja ॐ, which belongs to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa.

sandhi.note: -āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga (as रु) becomes y, and that y is dropped before a consonant (a further rule, not cited here by number), leaving -ā. The same change gives प्रणतिनम्रशिरोधरांसा before वाग्भिः.

Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra.
a + u → o (पुलक + उद्गम → पुलकोद्गम). Inside उद्गम the t of the prefix उत् is voiced before g (झलां जशोऽन्ते, 8.2.39).

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (शिरोधरांसाः) and a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (प्रणतिनम्र)
samasa.literal: whose necks and shoulders are bent by obeisance
samasa.alt: शिरोधरा ‘neck’ is itself a compound, शिरः धरति इति ‘that which holds the head’ (upapada); the whole is still one bahuvrīhi.

samasa.vigraha: पुलकानाम् उद्गमः पुलकोद्गमः; प्रहर्षेण (जातः) पुलकोद्गमः प्रहर्षपुलकोद्गमः; तेन चारवः देहाः येषां ते
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing tatpuruṣas (ṣaṣṭhī पुलकोद्गम; tṛtīyā प्रहर्षपुलकोद्गम)
samasa.literal: whose bodies are beautiful with the rising of hair-thrills from great joy

morph.note: Perfect of √स्तु: reduplication तु-स्तु-, the root’s s becomes ṣ after the u of the reduplicated syllable and the t then becomes ṭ beside it (ष्टुना ष्टुः, 8.4.41); before the vowel ending -उस् the root’s u becomes uv: तुष्टुवुः ‘they praised’.
Locative absolute: participle and noun in the locative (तस्मिन् … निहते) state the circumstance ‘when he had been slain’; the agent देव्या stands in the instrumental.
Instrumental plural of वाच्: before the ending -भिः the final c becomes k and is then voiced to g (झलां जशोऽन्ते, 8.2.39).

mantras.anvaya: तस्मिन् अतिवीर्ये दुरात्मनि सुरारिबले च देव्या निहते, प्रणतिनम्रशिरोधरांसाः प्रहर्षपुलकोद्गमचारुदेहाः शक्रादयः सुरगणाः तां वाग्भिः तुष्टुवुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A locative absolute (तस्मिन् … सुरारिबले च देव्या निहते) sets the time; the main clause is शक्रादयः सुरगणाः तां तुष्टुवुः, with two bahuvrīhi epithets of the gods and the instrument वाग्भिः.
mantras.lit: When that one of surpassing valour, the evil-souled, and the army of the gods’ enemies had been slain by the Devī, the hosts of the gods, Śakra and the rest, their necks and shoulders bent low in reverence, their bodies beautiful with hair standing on end for joy, praised her with words.
mantras.tr: When the Devī had slain that mighty, evil-hearted one and the army of the gods’ enemies, Indra and the hosts of the gods, necks and shoulders bowed in reverence, their bodies thrilling with joy, praised her in words.
mantras.tr_note: ‘That one’ (तस्मिन्) is Mahiṣāsura, who is named only in 4.12.

comm.t: The narrative frame of the hymn: Medhas tells how the gods praised the Devī after Mahiṣa’s death (3.42–44). With this stanza the text changes metre: 4.2–4.23 are in vasantatilakā, a fourteen-syllable quarter printed one quarter to a line, so a word can run over a line-end (as in 4.7–4.10); 4.24–4.27 return to anuṣṭubh.

The chapter’s colophon names it शक्रादिस्तुतिः, ‘the praise by Śakra and the others’, after the first word of this stanza. The bodily signs — bowing and the thrill of joy (pulaka) — are the classical marks of devotion: the praise is offered by the whole person, not only in words.

sandhi.note: ततम् keeps its m before the vowel of इदम्; इदम् shows anusvāra before j; the t of जगत् becomes d before the vowel ā.

The visarga of निः becomes s before the sibilant and the s becomes ś beside ś: निश्शेष. Visarga before a sibilant may also simply stay (an optional rule): निःशेष, the reading of GRETIL and Freund (corrections.json, variant).

samasa.sense: by her own power, needing nothing outside her

samasa.vigraha: निश्शेषाः देवगणाः; निश्शेषदेवगणानां शक्तयः; तासां समूहः; सः मूर्तिः यस्याः सा, तया
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣas (…शक्ति, …समूह) and a karmadhāraya (निश्शेषदेवगण)
samasa.literal: whose form is the mass of the powers of the entire hosts of gods
samasa.sense: the Devī whose body was formed from the gathered energies of all the gods (2.10–19)
samasa.alt: It can also be read as a karmadhāraya qualifying आत्मशक्त्या: ‘by her own power, which is the embodied mass of the gods’ powers’. The feminine i-stem ending fits either; the bahuvrīhi, describing the Devī herself, matches chapter 2.

samasa.literal: from which the remainder has gone

samasa.vigraha: देवाः च महर्षयः च देवमहर्षयः; अखिलैः देवमहर्षिभिः पूज्या, ताम्
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (with the gerundive पूज्य) containing an itaretara dvandva (देवमहर्षि); महर्षि is a karmadhāraya (महान् ऋषिः)
samasa.literal: to be worshipped by all the gods and great sages
samasa.sense: honoured by every god and seer

morph.note: Past passive participle of √तन्: the root’s nasal is lost before the participle ending (तन् + त → तत). With no copula expressed, ततम् is a finite-like predicate: ‘(this world) is pervaded’.
Imperative third singular of वि + √धा, a reduplicating (juhotyādi) root: दधा- + तु. ‘May she grant’ — the benediction that closes the first stanza.

The metre (vasantatilakā, ⏑ in the fifth syllable) needs a light syllable here, so the printed स्म cannot be a sandhi form of स्मः (which would give स्मो before v). The same phrase returns in 4.5 (नताः स्म परिपालय).

mantras.anvaya: यया निश्शेषदेवगणशक्तिसमूहमूर्त्या देव्या आत्मशक्त्या इदं जगत् ततम्, तां अखिलदेवमहर्षिपूज्याम् अम्बिकां (वयं) भक्त्या नताः स्म। सा नः शुभानि विदधातु।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यया … ततम्) describes the Devī; the main clause (ताम् … नताः स्म) is the act of bowing; a separate benediction with the imperative विदधातु closes the stanza.
mantras.lit: To that Ambikā, worthy of worship by all gods and great sages — the Devī, whose form is the mass of the powers of all the hosts of gods, by whom through her own power this world is pervaded — we are bowed with devotion. May she bestow auspicious things on us.
mantras.tr: To Ambikā, worshipped by all the gods and great sages — the Devī who by her own power pervades this world, her form the gathered powers of all the hosts of gods — we bow in devotion. May she grant us what is good.
mantras.tr_note: The passive ‘by whom … is pervaded’ is turned active; ‘we bow’ renders नताः स्म.

comm.t: The first stanza of praise recalls how the Devī came to be: her body was formed from the tejas of all the gods (2.10–19). Yet the world is pervaded by her own power (आत्मशक्त्या): what the gods gave was not borrowed strength. The gods bow and ask for blessings (शुभानि).

The prayer विदधातु शुभानि सा नः has an echo in the gods’ hymn of chapter 5 (5.81: करोतु सा नः शुभहेतुरीश्वरी शुभानि). The name Ambikā, ‘Mother’, is the one the text uses most often for the warrior Goddess.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the name Ambikā (name 295, अम्बिका). The two works are separate; the name is shared Śākta usage.

flags.uncertain: Variant: निश्शेष (Gita Press, kept) against निःशेष (GRETIL, Freund) — orthographic only, same word. Interpretation: नताः स्म is taken in the usual sense ‘we are bowed’ (स्म for स्मः, the visarga absent, as the metre requires); it may also be the particle स्म with the bare participle (‘bowed indeed’). The sense is the same.

sandhi.type: final n before a vowel; visarga sandhi
sandhi.note: After the long ā the final n is not doubled (ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्, 8.3.32, needs a short vowel); it is simply written with the vowel. अनन्तः before the voiced b of ब्रह्मा becomes अनन्तो.

sandhi.note: वक्तुम् keeps its m before the vowel of अलम्; अलम् and बलम् show anusvāra before b and c.

samasa.literal: that which has no balance (to weigh it against)

samasa.sense: Ananta — here Viṣṇu, beside Brahmā and Hara
samasa.alt: Ananta is also the name of Śeṣa, the serpent with a thousand mouths; the triad with Brahmā and Hara favours Viṣṇu.

samasa.vigraha: अखिलं जगत् अखिलजगत्; अखिलजगतः परिपालनम्, तस्मै
samasa.literal: for the protection of the whole world

samasa.vigraha: अशुभं च भयं च अशुभभयम्, तस्य
samasa.alt: Also read as a pañcamī tatpuruṣa, अशुभात् भयम्, ‘fear arising from evil’. The sense is close; the dvandva is the more common reading.

morph.note: Infinitive of √वच् (वच् + तुम्, c → k before t). With अलम् it expresses capacity: न … वक्तुम् अलम् ‘not able to tell’; the verb ‘are’ is understood.
Imperative third singular of √कृ: stem करो- (tanādi u-class) + तु. मतिं करोतु ‘may she set her mind on’.
Nominative singular of भगवत् (भग + matup → -वत्): the vowel before the -nt is lengthened and the final t lost: भगवान्.

mantras.anvaya: यस्याः अतुलं प्रभावं बलं च भगवान् अनन्तः ब्रह्मा हरः च वक्तुं न हि अलम्, सा चण्डिका अखिलजगत्परिपालनाय अशुभभयस्य नाशाय च मतिं करोतु।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यस्याः … अलम्, the verb ‘are’ understood) and its correlative main clause (सा चण्डिका … करोतु); two datives of purpose depend on मतिं करोतु.
mantras.lit: Whose incomparable majesty and strength the Blessed Ananta, Brahmā and Hara are indeed not able to tell — may that Caṇḍikā set her mind on the protection of the whole world and on the destruction of evil and fear.
mantras.tr: Her incomparable majesty and strength not even blessed Viṣṇu, Brahmā or Śiva can describe. May that Caṇḍikā turn her mind to protecting the whole world and to ending evil and fear.
mantras.tr_note: Ananta and Hara are named as Viṣṇu and Śiva; ‘not even’ renders the emphatic न हि.

comm.t: The three great gods of the triad cannot describe her power; the lesser gods therefore do not try to measure her but ask her to act. The prayer has two aims: protection (परिपालन) and the removal of evil and fear.

The thought that even Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva cannot describe the Goddess is a commonplace of Śākta hymns; the next stanzas (4.6–4.7) develop it. Caṇḍikā, ‘the Fierce One’, is the name from which the whole text takes its popular title, the Caṇḍī.
